- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 7–14 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85% of recent high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for next 5–10 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 80+), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day for next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment turns bearish, forecast should slope down).  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; reduce first 5–7 forecast points by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
